source.title: Momentum in large-batch training: Polyak enlarges the critical batch size, Nesterov improves data efficiency
source.authors: Jia-Nan Wang; Zi-Xun Huang; Kai-Rui Li; Lei Wu

record.file_problem: Full paper text, including appendices, is present.
record.tranche_reason: Tests batch-size and optimizer effects on held-out performance in ImageNet-1K training and stability in CIFAR-10, extending the large-batch training question to these neural-network settings. Its main PLK regression results are on a tractable regression model, not the natural-label generalization claim.
record.gate_note: The paper reports optimizer comparisons of validation loss and stability boundaries in neural-network experiments, plus PLK regression results on excess risk. Rows capture the reported held-out ImageNet comparison and the explicit CIFAR-10 stability statements. Theoretical PLK scaling laws and figure-only comparisons without textual values are not reconstructed as result rows.
record.test_reason: The ImageNet experiment measures held-out cross-entropy across batch sizes under the same three-epoch budget, directly bearing on V5. It extends the comparison to tuned Polyak and Nesterov momentum with group normalization. CIFAR-10 stability and synthetic kernel-regression results do not test the listed versions.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is accurate. The authors conclude that Polyak permits fewer sequential updates through larger batches while preserving data efficiency, whereas Nesterov can improve data efficiency in the large-batch regime. These are theoretical and quantitative findings in PLK regression; ImageNet supplies qualitative held-out-loss evidence and CIFAR-10 supplies qualitative stability evidence.
record.recipe_differences: The study investigates momentum's batch-size effects using PLK regression theory and experiments, plus ResNet-18 on ImageNet-1K and CIFAR-10. Its neural-network ImageNet recipe uses a fixed three-epoch sample budget, grid-searches learning rate and momentum, and omits warmup, weight decay and label smoothing; this is not the original large-batch generalization-gap protocol.
record.method_sensitivity: The reported outcomes vary with optimizer and batch size. On CIFAR-10, stability boundaries also vary with batch size and momentum damping, with saturation and earlier Nesterov saturation stated.

fits_no_version.finding: CIFAR-10 learning-rate stability boundaries grow and saturate differently across SGD, Polyak and Nesterov.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: For ResNet-18 with group normalization, momentum changes the dependence of stable learning rates on batch size and momentum damping.

fits_no_version.finding: PLK regression theory and simulations show optimizer-dependent critical batch sizes, excess-risk dynamics and data-scaling exponents.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: In noisy one-pass power-law kernel regression, Polyak extends the batch range preserving small-batch data efficiency, while Nesterov can improve the large-batch data-scaling exponent.

record.problems: Neural-network evidence is qualitative; ImageNet values are presented in a plot without numeric values in the text. ImageNet uses one seed and only three epochs. CIFAR-10 stability is evaluated on training images, not held-out performance. The paper does not measure training–test gaps or test the claim's memorization premise.
record.rows_left_out: No separate rows for PLK regression theoretical scaling laws or its figure-only quantitative results: these measure excess risk in a tractable synthetic regression model rather than the natural-label train–test behavior in the claim. ImageNet Figure 9's numerical points are not transcribed because the supplied text gives only a plot; the prose-supported qualitative comparisons are included in R1–R3.

untested.parts: Random-label fitting and its coexistence with natural-label generalization.
Convolutional versus fully connected image classifiers and local connectivity.
Adaptive optimizers versus SGD; Polyak and Nesterov are momentum methods, not adaptive methods.

Language models; longer training; warmup and learning-rate schedules; controlled normalization or regularization changes; classification accuracy; and performance after conventional full training. Nesterov's large-batch loss relative to its own small-batch baseline is not established by the readable text.
Magnitude-aware sharpness and its ranking of generalization gaps.
Removing memorized examples versus random examples.

record.verdict_notes: This study is not an original source for any version. Validation cross-entropy is a held-out performance measure, so a training–test gap is unnecessary for testing V5. The ImageNet results select the lowest validation loss across completed stable configurations, use one shared seed and only three epochs, and provide no readable numerical losses or uncertainty estimates. Group normalization is used throughout, so its causal contribution is untested. Omitted PLK results and numerical plot points are already declared in rows_left_out.

versions.untested_parts: Random-label memorization and natural-label generalization coexistence are not tested.
No width sweep or interpolation-threshold test.
No convolutional versus fully connected comparison.

ImageNet-1K is tested with a fixed sample budget of three epochs; CIFAR-10 reports stability boundaries, not held-out performance. Language models, comparisons to smaller batches under fixed epoch budgets beyond the reported curves, and the effects of longer training, warmup, normalization or regularization changes are not tested.
No magnitude-aware sharpness or generalization-gap measurement.

rows.subject: ResNet-18
rows.operation_detail: Trained with SGD at each batch size; reports the lowest final validation cross-entropy among completed stable configurations.

conditions.value: without learning-rate warmup, weight decay, or label smoothing
lowest final validation cross-entropy among evaluated stable hyperparameter configurations

rows.baseline: Figure 9 plots the three optimizers across batch sizes; numeric baseline not stated.
rows.value: The text says Polyak maintains performance over a substantially larger batch-size range than SGD, and Nesterov attains lower risk than both in the large-batch regime; exact values are figure only.
rows.note: Textual description gives the qualitative optimizer and batch-size comparison; the figure contains the values, which are not transcribed as numbers.
rows.check: Section 7.2 describes the same qualitative batch-size dependence as the kernel experiment and says Polyak preserves SGD's best performance over a wider batch range, supporting an earlier large-batch penalty for SGD. Replace the comparative value with this within-SGD finding and use SGD's small-batch validation loss as baseline. Add group normalization, constant learning rate, and one shared seed to the conditions. Exact losses and transition batch sizes cannot be recovered from the supplied plot text.

rows.baseline: SGD at corresponding batch sizes; exact value not stated.
rows.value: Polyak achieves a best risk comparable to SGD, but maintains this performance over a substantially larger batch-size range; exact values are figure only.
rows.note: Text states the qualitative comparison; no precise validation-loss values are given in prose.
rows.check: The reported preservation of small-batch performance over a wider batch range directly measures V5's recipe-dependence qualification; it is not merely a partial effect. State Polyak's own best small-batch performance as the preservation baseline, with SGD as the comparison for range extension. Add group normalization, constant learning rate and momentum, and one shared seed.

rows.baseline: SGD and Polyak at corresponding batch sizes; exact values not stated.
rows.value: Nesterov attains lower risk than both SGD and Polyak in the large-batch regime; exact values are figure only.
rows.note: Text states the qualitative comparison; the figure provides no transcribed numerical values.
rows.check: Lower large-batch loss than SGD and Polyak establishes optimizer dependence, but alone does not establish whether Nesterov's large batches worsen, preserve, or improve its own small-batch performance. The supplied plot text does not resolve that comparison. Retain the comparative finding, replace the unsupported partial state, and add group normalization, constant learning rate and momentum, and one shared seed.

relationships.condition: SGD, ResNet-18 with group normalization on ImageNet-1K, fixed three-epoch budget
relationships.reason: R1 and Section 7.2 describe a large-batch deterioration occurring earlier for SGD than for Polyak, consistent with a workload-dependent batch threshold.
relationships.display_finding: The study reports earlier large-batch deterioration for SGD than Polyak momentum, but this comparison remains unverified.

relationships.condition: Tuned Polyak momentum, ResNet-18 on ImageNet-1K, fixed three-epoch budget
relationships.reason: R2 preserves comparable best validation loss over substantially larger batches, supporting V5's qualification that adapting the recipe can postpone the penalty.
relationships.display_finding: Tuned Polyak momentum reportedly preserved comparable validation loss over larger batches, but this comparison remains unverified.

relationships.condition: Choice of momentum method at large batches, ResNet-18 on ImageNet-1K
relationships.reason: R3 reports lower large-batch validation loss with Nesterov than with SGD or Polyak, showing optimizer-dependent outcomes; it does not establish improvement over Nesterov's own small-batch baseline.
relationships.display_finding: The reported lower validation loss with Nesterov remains unverified and does not establish improvement over its own small-batch baseline.
